title: Senior asks: another website runs fetch('http://your-api/?action=delete&file=a.csv', {method: 'DELETE'}) in a visitor's browser. Your API sets no CORS headers. What happens?
options: The browser first sends an OPTIONS preflight, gets no permission, and blocks the DELETE. The file stays.
The file is deleted. DELETE is the same as GET.
The file is deleted, but the other site cannot read the answer.
The API answers 200 and the browser deletes the file later.
explain: A DELETE request is not a simple request. The browser asks first with OPTIONS. Your API sends no Access-Control-Allow headers, so the browser stops before the real DELETE. This is why DELETE is safer than POST here. It is not real security: without auth, anyone can call the API with curl.

title: Senior asks: FileNotFoundException builds its message from the file name in the URL. Someone sends ?file=. Why is this harmless today, and when does it become dangerous?
options: Harmless because app.js shows messages with .text(). Dangerous if someone later uses .html() or Twig |raw.
Harmless because PHP removes all HTML tags from the URL.
Harmless because JSON can never contain the < character.
Dangerous today, because every error message is shown as HTML.
explain: .text() puts the string in the page as plain text, so the tag is only shown. The server does not clean the file name here. If a future change uses .html(), the same message runs as code (XSS). Escape at the place where you output, and review any change from .text() to .html().

title: Senior asks: there are no tests for FileNameResolver. What is a good first test?
options: Create a.csv in a temp folder, call reserveFreeName() for a.csv, expect a_1.csv. Call again, expect a_2.csv.
Test that fopen() works in PHP.
Mock FileNameResolver and check that it returns a string.
No test is needed: the class has only 20 lines.
explain: The loop that adds _1, _2 is the logic that can break and silently overwrite a file. A test with a real temp folder checks the loop and the 'x' create mode together. Mocking the class itself tests nothing. Short code can still hide a bug.

title: Senior asks: delete() first calls findFileActions($fileName) and ignores the result. Someone sends ?action=delete&file=notes.txt. What happens, and what is the side effect?
options: UnsupportedFormat error. The call works as a safety check: only .csv and .json files can be deleted.
The file is deleted, because the result is ignored.
FileNotFoundException, because .txt is never in storage/.
A fatal PHP error, because the return value is unused.
explain: findFileActions() throws when the extension has no handler, before unlink() runs. So the API cannot delete other files, for example .htaccess or a .php file. The call looks useless but protects. A comment or a method name like assertSupported() would make this clear to the next reader.

title: What does Node print?
options: object number object
null number array
object NaN array
null NaN object
explain: typeof null is 'object' (an old bug that stays for compatibility). typeof NaN is 'number'. typeof [] is 'object', not 'array'. Use Array.isArray(x) for arrays and x === null for null.

title: What does this print?
options: E 1
E 2
explain: readonly protects the property from change after construction, and that includes $c->items[] = 2. PHP throws Error, so we print E. The array still has 1 item. To add an item, make a new object with a new array (withItem()).

title: PHP 8. What does this print?
explain: / gives a float when the result is not whole: 3.5. intdiv() cuts toward zero: 3. % returns the remainder, and its sign follows the left number: -7 % 3 is -1, not 2. For page counts use intdiv() or ceil() on purpose.

title: git pull stops with a conflict. In the file you see <<<<<<< HEAD, =======, >>>>>>>. What do you do?
options: Edit the file to the final text, remove the three marker lines, git add the file, then commit (or continue the rebase).
Commit the file as it is. Git will clean the markers.
Run git pull again until the markers go away.
Delete the file and pull again.
explain: The markers show both versions. Git cannot choose for you. You decide the final text, delete the markers, then git add marks the conflict as solved. Always run the tests before you commit: a merge can compile and still be wrong. Never commit the marker lines.
